text.text: A tour is a sales meeting in disguise. Let people imagine their day before you talk about price.
Before they arrive
Room set up the way they want to see it
Lights, music and heating on
A one-page price guide and the calendar for their dates
During the tour
Ask what they picture: arrival, ceremony, dinner, dancing.
Walk the route a guest would take, and stop where they will stand.
Mention what is included, and what needs a vendor.
Answer questions honestly, including noise and finish times.
Afterwards
Offer a hold on the date for a set number of days.
Log the tour notes and set a follow-up for the next working day.
Holds
A hold lasts seven days unless the director approves more.
Every hold has an expiry date; the Dashboard lists them.
Never hold two dates in the same space for the same day.
Contracts
Send the contract with the fee, deposit, balance date and rules.
Move the booking to Contracted when signed.
Press Record deposit when payment arrives.
Cancellations
Follow the contract terms. Note the date of any cancellation request and who received it.
Two hours before
Doors unlocked, heating or cooling set
Restrooms stocked and checked
Layout matches the diagram
Vendors arriving per the schedule
During
Event manager is on site from first vendor to last guest.
Keep a phone number for the host and caterer at hand.
After
Walk the space and photograph any damage.
Count rentals and clear waste.
Press Close out and collect the balance if due.
What every client hears
Music must end by the time in the contract; the hall closes thirty minutes later.
Open flames are not allowed except in the candle holders we supply.
Decorations may be taped only to the boards we provide.
Outside caterers must be approved and insured.
Why we say it
Rules are easier to follow when the reason is clear: neighbors, floors, safety and the next booking.
Exceptions
Anything unusual goes in the booking page and is approved by the director before the contract is signed.
